title: Multidimensional arrays and row/column traversal
learningObjectives: Explain the language rule and its constraints.
Trace the example and predict its output.
Identify relevant boundary and safety cases.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: A two-dimensional array is an array of row arrays. For int grid[2][3], valid row indices are 0–1 and column indices are 0–2. C stores rows contiguously in row-major order.
understand.whyItMatters: This concept supports correct handling of C data and helps prevent invalid memory access or incorrect program behaviour.
understand.analogy: Think of the construct as a precisely bounded sequence of storage and operations.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's rules for object lifetime, bounds, types or undefined behaviour.

explain.narrative:
A two-dimensional array is an array of row arrays. For int grid[2][3], valid row indices are 0–1 and column indices are 0–2. C stores rows contiguously in row-major order.

Always check the types, object bounds and preconditions required by the operation. Compile with warnings enabled and test ordinary as well as boundary inputs.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: The outer loop selects a row and the inner loop visits its columns. The output is two rows: 1 2 3 and 4 5 6.

practise.guidedTask: Draw a 2-by-3 grid and label each element with its row and column index.
practise.independentTask: Calculate each row's sum in a 3-by-4 matrix and test every boundary.
hints: Use bounds separately for each dimension.
When passing a 2D array to a function, later dimension sizes are part of the parameter type.
C multidimensional arrays are arrays of arrays, not automatically resizable matrices.
